comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming operating income decreased to $290 million in 2024 from $971 million in 2023, primarily driven by lower revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze segment financial performance drivers, though AMD focuses on operating income decline due to lower revenue while Intel focuses on cost of sales reduction. AMD's Gaming segment operating income dropped to $290 million primarily due to lower revenue. Intel's DCAI cost of sales decreased by $661 million due to lower server sales volume and reserves. Both reflect the sensitivity of semiconductor segment financials to sales volume and market demand, but contrast Intel's cost control/efficiency gains with AMD's revenue contraction in a different segment.

sentences.text: ▪DCAI cost of sales decreased $661 million from 2022, primarily driven by lower server sales volume, lower sample costs, and lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves taken in 2023. These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 7 products sold in 2023.
Gaming operating income was $290 million in 2024, compared to operating income of $971 million in 2023.
The decrease in operating income was primarily driven by lower revenue.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor Solutions segment operating income drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating income from the semiconductor solutions segment increased, primarily driven by revenue growth from networking products (including AI networking products), partially offset by lower net revenue from broadband and server storage products.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies analyze segment operating income drivers in the context of AI product demand and cost dynamics. Intel reports DCAI cost of sales changes linked to an increased mix of Intel 7 products and server sales volume. Broadcom reports semiconductor solutions segment operating income growth driven by AI networking product revenue, partially offset by lower revenue in other areas. While Intel focuses on the cost side (cost of sales) and Broadcom on the income side (operating income), both identify AI-related product mix and demand as key operational drivers influencing financial results in their respective segments.

These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 7 products sold in 2023.

Operating income from our semiconductor solutions segment increased mainly driven by revenue growth from networking products, primarily AI networking products, partially offset by lower net revenue from our broadband and server storage products.

comparisons.peer_summary: EBU operating income decreased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to declines in average selling prices, partially offset by higher bit shipments and cost reductions.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss operating income drivers for semiconductor segments, specifically highlighting cost reductions as a mitigating factor for other negative trends, though in opposite directions relative to revenue/pricing. Intel's DCAI cost of sales decreased significantly due to volume and reserve changes, while Micron's EBU operating income decreased due to lower average selling prices, partially offset by cost reductions. Both reflect the interplay between unit economics (volume/mix/pricing) and cost management in semiconductor manufacturing, but Intel focuses on absolute cost of sales decrease while Micron focuses on the margin compression from pricing amidst cost efficiencies.

• EBU operating income decreased primarily due to declines in average selling prices, partially offset by higher bit shipments and cost reductions.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, or for obsolete or excess inventory and excess product purchase commitments, requiring management judgment based on inventory levels, future commitments, and market conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their accounting policy for cost of sales related to inventory provisions and write-downs. Intel details a $661 million decrease in DCAI cost of sales driven by lower reserves and period charges from inventory sell-through, indicating the operational impact of these policies. Similarly, NVIDIA describes its policy of charging cost of sales for inventory provisions to write down inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, noting that these provisions often relate to excess quantities based on management judgment of future demand. While Intel reports the specific financial outcome of reduced reserves, NVIDIA explains the general mechanism and judgment required for such provisions, addressing the same underlying cost of sales component.

sentences.text: ▪DCAI cost of sales decreased $661 million from 2022, primarily driven by lower server sales volume, lower sample costs, and lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves taken in 2023. These cost of sales decreases were partially offset by higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 7 products sold in 2023.

We charge cost of sales for inventory provisions to write-down our inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value or for obsolete or excess inventory, and for excess product purchase commitments.

Most of our inventory provisions relate to excess quantities of products or components, based on our inventory levels and future product purchase commitments compared to assumptions about future demand and market conditions, which requires management judgment.

comparisons.peer_summary: QTL EBT as a percentage of revenues increased in fiscal 2024 primarily due to lower cost of sales driven by a decrease in amortization expense related to acquired patents and higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies analyze drivers of cost of sales changes within their respective segments. Intel attributes a $661 million decrease in Data Center and AI cost of sales to lower period charges from reserved inventory sell-through and lower reserves. Qualcomm identifies that its QTL segment's EBT margin expansion was partially due to lower cost of sales driven by a decrease in amortization expense related to acquired patents. Although the specific cost drivers differ (inventory reserves vs. patent amortization), both disclosures explicitly link changes in cost of sales components to financial performance metrics in Item 7.
